profile.stagger_pattern: THREE-YEAR terms, two groups on the Texas May uniform date (first Saturday in May). Group A = Districts 1-4, elected 2018, 2021, 2024, 2027. Group B = Mayor, Super District 5, Super District 6, elected 2019, 2022, 2025, 2028. No city general election falls in 2020, 2023 or 2026. Verified against seven consecutive ACFR 'Elected Officials' pages (FY2019-FY2025), whose 'Term Expires' columns read May 2021/May 2022 (FY2019-20), May 2024/May 2022 (FY2021), May 2024/May 2025 (FY2022-23), May 2027/May 2025 (FY2024) and May 2027/May 2028 (FY2025), plus the city's own election pages for May 4 2024 (Districts 1-4), May 3 2025 (Districts 5, 6 and Mayor) and May 1 2027 (Districts 1-4).

run_log.detail: Registry said Victoria's calendar/term/stagger were UNVERIFIED and that victoriatx.gov robots.txt connect-times-out. BOTH victoriatx.org and victoriatx.gov served robots.txt and every page to plain curl with a browser UA on first try - the .gov timeout did not reproduce. Registry's Clarity/ES&S warning held: no county results portal was used. TML directory not used.

STRUCTURE SETTLED FROM SOURCE, and it is unusual: Victoria uses THREE-YEAR terms, not 2 or 4. Two groups on the May uniform date - Districts 1-4 (2018, 2021, 2024, 2027) and Mayor + Super District 5 + Super District 6 (2019, 2022, 2025, 2028). Established from the 'Term Expires' column of seven consecutive ACFR Elected Officials pages plus the city's own May 2024 / May 2025 / May 2027 election pages. Consequence: FOUR general cycles fall in the 2019-2026 panel (2019, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025 - five counting both groups), and 2020, 2023 and 2026 have no city general election at all. Mayor is directly elected at large (ACFR: 'a Mayor, who is elected at large, and six Council Members elected by district'); Mayor Pro Tem is chosen by the council (2022 Charter Proposition G: elected at the first regular meeting following each regular city election). Council-manager form. 7 elected seats: Mayor, Districts 1-4, Super Districts 5-6.

PRIMARY UNLOCK: the CivicPlus Archive Center at /Archive.aspx?AMID=41 holds the full ACFR/CAFR series 2008-2023, fetched as /ArchiveCenter/ViewFile/Item/{ADID} (FY2019=75, FY2020=191, FY2021=195, FY2022=201); FY2023/24/25 are in DocumentCenter (13938, 16706, 19383). Every one carries an 'ELECTED OFFICIALS' page naming all seven seats with district, years of service and term-expiry - a complete Sept-30 snapshot for every panel year 2019-2025. The site search /Search/Results?searchPhrase= found the recent three but NOT the older four; only the Archive Center did. City election canvass PDFs (DocumentCenter 16888, 13435, 18743) are image-only scans with no text layer.

Six mid-term changes found and dated. (1) Mayor Rawley McCoy DIED unexpectedly 2021-03-05, 22 months into a term running to May 2022. (2) A special mayoral election was held Saturday 2021-07-03 (within the charter's 120-day window); Jeff Bauknight won outright with 69.39% over Emett Alvarez (25.52%) and David Crook (5.1%). The mayoralty was vacant 2021-03-05 to mid-July 2021; Mayor Pro Tem Josephine Soliz would have presided. (3) Bauknight had just won re-election to District 3 on 2021-05-01 (1,792 to Aaron Franco's 460) and vacated that seat to run for mayor, so District 3 was on the same 2021-07-03 special ballot; no majority, and Crocker beat Hall in a RUNOFF on 2021-08-21. (4) Duane Crocker was sworn in to District 3 on Tuesday 2021-09-07 - District 3 sat vacant roughly July to September 2021. (5) Mayor Bauknight announced for Texas House District 30 on 2023-11-13, which under Texas Const. art. XVI sec. 65(b) is an AUTOMATIC RESIGNATION; he held over until a successor qualified, and the FY2023 ACFR still lists him as mayor at 2023-09-30. (6) Crocker won the 2024-02-03 special mayoral election (six candidates, incl. Josephine Soliz) without a runoff and was sworn in Tuesday 2024-02-20, vacating District 3 a second time; District 3 stayed vacant until April Butler was seated after the 2024-05-04 general. All in-panel vacancies fall inside seat-years that already carry a sourced tenure on either side, so they are recorded here rather than as gap rows.

Day-of-week checks pass: 2019-05-04, 2021-05-01, 2021-07-03, 2021-08-21, 2022-05-07, 2024-02-03, 2024-05-04 and 2025-05-03 are all Saturdays (Texas uniform/authorized election dates); 2019-05-07, 2021-09-07, 2024-02-20 and 2024-05-21 are all Tuesdays (council meets 1st and 3rd Tuesday). CAUTION RECORDED: the ACFR 'Years of Service' column is unreliable - the FY2023 edition credits Duane Crocker with 4 years when he was sworn in 2021-09-07 (2 years). The 'Term Expires' column and the name/district pairing were consistent across all seven editions and are what the reconstruction rests on. UNCERTAIN BOUNDARIES, all flagged in confidence: (a) Bauknight's mayoral start is set to 2021-07-13, the council meeting that certified the July 3 results, not a sourced swearing-in date; (b) Kidder's and Butler's start and Soliz's District 2 end are set to 2024-05-21, the third-Tuesday meeting at which the Advocate reported new members were sworn in; (c) the Mayor Pro Tem chain is anchored only on ACFR snapshots - Soliz was selected 2019-05-07 (sourced), Young held it at 2022-09-30, Soliz again at 2023-09-30, Young at 2024-09-30, 2025-09-30 and now. The two middle handovers have no sourced date and are marked LOW confidence with nominal May boundaries; the 2023 switch is anomalous because no election fell in 2023. (d) Who held Mayor Pro Tem before 2019-05-07 was not established; the seat-year is covered by Soliz from May 2019.

victoriaadvocate.com fetches cleanly to curl with a browser UA - no 403, no paywall interception, and NO ROT47/ROT13 obfuscation (article bodies are plain text, including 'premium' URLs). Its WordPress REST API is open and was the highest-yield tool of the run: /wp-json/wp/v2/posts?search=&after=&before=&per_page=&_fields=date,link,title returned dated headline lists that pinned every 2021 and 2024 mid-term event without a single search-engine query. Municode's code library returns a JavaScript shell to curl and was abandoned; the charter text was not needed because the ACFR series and the city's own election pages settled the structure. The CivicWeb portal (victoriatx.civicweb.net) is reachable and its meeting list parses, but meeting ids are non-chronological across bodies and it was not needed once the ACFR series was found.
8 seat labels x 8 years = 64 seat-years, all covered by tenures; no gap rows.
